journey.name: usdt payment links and scans
journey.description: Use an onboarded wallet with USDT configured and another owned wallet's Arbitrum receive URI. No payment is submitted. Hardware-wallet send remains Bitcoin-only.

actions.action: Enable USDT in the introductory sheet or Settings, General, Payments before starting this flow.

Open an ethereum: USDT receive link with chain 42161, the pinned Arbitrum token, an owned recipient and uint256=10001. Verify the USDT amount screen preserves the recipient and exact input 0.010001 USDT; the review rounds its displayed value to $0.01. Verify no payment occurs without approval.

Copy the USDT receive URI, return to Home and accept the clipboard prompt. Verify the USDT amount screen opens with the copied recipient and amount. Cancel without paying. Repeat with a wrong-chain URI and verify no payment prompt appears.

Cancel the send and remain on the USDT wallet without returning Home, then reopen the identical URI. Verify the amount or review screen opens again. Cancel back to the USDT wallet and open a different owned recipient and amount, verifying only the new values appear.

Close the send sheet, open Settings from the drawer, then go back. Verify the dismissed link does not reopen its Amount screen. Explicitly reopen the same link and verify a new send flow is available, then cancel without paying.

While a USDT contact amount screen, contact review or direct-send review is open, open another USDT link, then scan or accept a clipboard prompt for another owned bare USDT address. Verify the active recipient, amount and contact or request are preserved, with no new send flow or invalid-QR error. Where PIN is enabled, repeat while its approval screen is visible, then cancel without paying.
Open USDT from Home, open a USDT link, then open a second link with another owned recipient and amount. Verify the first amount and recipient remain. Cancel without paying.
Cancel the send. Open the same link without uint256. Verify the amount screen opens with no amount and accepts a new amount.
Cancel the send. From the main scanner, paste or import a QR containing the same amount-bearing URI. Verify it opens the USDT send flow with the same recipient and amount.

Cancel the send. From the ordinary Send options, paste the URI. Verify it opens the USDT send flow. Cancel, choose Enter Manually, enter the same URI and continue. Verify the USDT recipient and exact amount are preserved. Repeat with a wrong-chain URI and in hardware-wallet Send; verify neither opens a USDT payment. In hardware-wallet manual entry, verify the Bitcoin-address-required warning appears and Continue stays disabled. Replace the URI with a valid Bitcoin address and verify Continue becomes available. Cancel, then open Send again from the USDT wallet and verify the previous recipient and amount are cleared.

Open or scan variants with the wrong chain, wrong token, duplicate amount and malformed recipient. Verify an error and no payable review. Check an ordinary Bitcoin or Lightning invoice still opens its existing send flow.

On iOS, open a USDT link while Lightning is stopped but the wallet is ready. Verify it routes without starting Lightning. Open two different USDT links while the main scanner sheet is dismissing; verify an older delayed link cannot replace the review that opened first.

Enter this wallet’s own Arbitrum address in USDT Send, enter an amount and continue. Verify the error explicitly says you cannot send USDT to your own address, and no payment is submitted. Repeat with MAX. On Android, enter this wallet’s own bare Arbitrum address through Home Send → Enter Manually and verify the self-send message appears while Continue stays disabled.

Enter the entire available USDT balance and continue. Verify the fee-collection error explains that the transaction fee could not be paid in USDT and suggests a smaller amount. Reduce the amount, reach review and close without signing.

With an empty wallet and no pending transfers, turn USDT off in Settings. Copy an owned bare USDT address, return to the app, and verify no automatic payment or enable prompt. Repeat with an amount-bearing USDT payment URI. Copy a valid Bitcoin address and a Lightning invoice in turn; verify their normal clipboard prompts still appear and cancel without paying.

With USDT off, explicitly open the same USDT URI and verify the designed Enable USDT modal appears. Decline and verify a quiet return with no stuck spinner. Scan its QR, enable USDT, and verify the original recipient and exact amount resume. Cancel without paying.
